evals.prompt:
Review this Go package design:

package store

type Store interface {
    GetReservation(ctx context.Context, id string) (*Reservation, error)
    SaveReservation(ctx context.Context, r *Reservation) error
    GetGuest(ctx context.Context, id string) (*Guest, error)
    SaveGuest(ctx context.Context, g *Guest) error
    GetFolio(ctx context.Context, id string) (*Folio, error)
}

A billing package only needs to look up a reservation by ID. Should billing depend on the Store interface above?
evals.expected_output: Flags that the interface is defined next to its implementation and is too large for the billing consumer, and recommends billing declare its own small consumer-side interface with just the method it needs.

assertions.text: Flags that the interface is too large / not scoped to what billing needs

evals.prompt: We have `func NewClient(url string) *Client` used across a dozen call sites. We now need to let some callers configure a custom timeout, without breaking the existing call sites. What's the safe way to extend this Go constructor?
evals.expected_output: Recommends the functional-options pattern (variadic Option parameters) so existing NewClient(url) calls keep compiling, rather than adding a required parameter.

assertions.text: Recommends functional options / variadic Option parameters
Notes existing call sites must keep working unchanged

evals.prompt: We want to add a new method to an exported Go interface that is implemented by three other internal packages and one open-source plugin outside our repo. Is this a safe change to make directly?
evals.expected_output: Flags that adding a method to an interface implemented outside the package is a breaking change for every implementer, especially the external plugin, and recommends an additive alternative such as a new interface or a new optional method surfaced via a separate type.

assertions.text: Flags this as a breaking change for implementers
Calls out the external/outside-repo implementer as the specific risk
